nameOrigin.text: Platteville was named for the nearby South Platte River.

founded.text: Founded in 1871, after the Denver Pacific Railroad reached the area.

timeline.text: Louis Vasquez and Andrew Sublette built Fort Vasquez, a fur trading post about one mile south of present-day Platteville.
St. Vrain, about four miles north of the present town, was designated the county seat when Weld County was established.
The Denver Pacific Railroad line from Evans to Denver was completed, and Johnson Station was established two miles south of the present town.
The Platte River Land Company filed a map of the Town of Platteville with the Colorado Territorial government on July 17.
The Platteville Pioneer Museum was started on the site of the previous town library.
